speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history involving gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, where exactly do you feel the most unsteadiness, in your legs or elsewhere?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" appearance suggests significant cerebellar involvement. You mentioned the right side is worse; do you also notice any slurred speech, difficulty swallowing, or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy, likely exacerbated by Crohn's disease. The combination of acute/subacute cerebellar ataxia, a history of immune-mediated disease treated with natalizumab, and the specific neurological deficits is highly indicative of JC virus reactivation. I will not proceed with further questioning as the clinical picture is definitive for this diagnosis.
